title: α- and β-D-glucose
back: Anomers differ only at C1: –OH down in α, up in β. Pyranose ring from the C5 –OH adding to C1.

title: α-Helix and β-sheet
back: Secondary structure, held by backbone N–H···O=C hydrogen bonds: within one chain (helix) or between chains (sheet).

title: DNA double helix
back: Two complementary strands; A=T (2 H-bonds), G≡C (3 H-bonds); sugar–phosphate backbone outside, bases inside.

title: Open-chain glucose
back: Nitric acid gives saccharic acid (primary –CH₂OH); oxime and cyanohydrin show the carbonyl.

title: Why glucose must be cyclic
legend: explanation = C5–OH and C1 form a hemiacetal ring
back: The pentaacetate also does not react with hydroxylamine: no free –CHO.

title: Sucrose, maltose, lactose
back: Sucrose: glucose C1–fructose C2. Maltose: 2 α-glucose C1–C4. Lactose: galactose + glucose C1–C4. Sucrose hydrolysis gives invert sugar.

title: Starch vs cellulose
back: Starch = amylose (unbranched) + amylopectin (branched); cellulose = straight β-chains; glycogen = more branched animal starch.

title: Zwitterion
back: Makes amino acids salt-like, high-melting and amphoteric. All except glycine are optically active.

title: Peptide bond
legend: formed = –COOH of one + –NH₂ of next, losing H₂O
back: Primary structure = sequence of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

title: Denaturation
back: Heat or pH breaks H-bonds; activity is lost. Examples: boiled egg, curdled milk.

title: Vitamin deficiencies
tex: \text{A: night blindness}\quad\text{C: scurvy}\quad\text{D: rickets}\quad\ce{B12}\text{: pernicious anaemia}
back: $\ce{B1}$ beriberi, $\ce{B2}$ cheilosis, $\ce{B6}$ convulsions, E fragile red cells, K slow clotting.

title: DNA vs RNA
back: DNA stores information; RNA (m, r, t) carries out protein synthesis.

title: ADEK = a deck
back: Stored in fat (a deck kept in the drawer); B and C are water-soluble and excreted.
